messages:
deploy-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated error rate for model-serving on gpu-pool-7 -> kernel OOB on pinned GPU buffers (cuda error). auto-escalation to #incidents at 2026-03-10T14:26:39Z :rotating_light:

ajay (oncall): seeing container restarts on node gpu-7-3, ~15% of requests 500-ing. linking recent deploy? @maria (infra) can you confirm node status?

maria (infra): node is flapping, kubelet shows repeated OOM/killed-container events and GPU driver errors in dmesg. I see "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" followed by a device reset. Not a typical memory pressure pattern.

kelsey (runtime): getting CUDA illegal memory access reports from runtime logs:
```
2026-03-10T14:21:07Z runtime[pid=2234]: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: misaligned access in pinned buffer copy at tensor-slab.cc:442
stack: Runtime::Execute -> TensorSlab::CopyToPinned -> memcpy_async -> kernel_launch(...)
```
This stack looks like something touches freed pinned host memory after eviction. Might be race when reusing pinned buffers across inference workers.

liz_sre: Customer impact: two PLG tenants in us-west-2 saw failed inference calls and retries. Estimated 1200 requests failed in the last 10m. No data exfiltration. Communicating to CS to notify impacted customers.

ajay (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: cordon gpu-7-3, drain pods, force-schedule away from pool, scale down replicas on that node group, enable model fallback to cpu-quantized variant. Kelsey, can runtime gate reuse of pinned buffers quickly?

kelsey (runtime): will flip a hotfix flag to disable pinned-buffer pooling on the affected runtime fleet. Patch will reduce perf but should stop OOB. Pushing config now: `RUNTIME_DISABLE_PINNED_POOL=true` to configmap serving-runtime/flags.

maria (infra): running drain now: `kubectl cordon gpu-7-3 && kubectl drain gpu-7-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30`
cmd output: pods evicted, but one model-pod stuck terminating due to a driver hang. Forcing container kill.

ops-bridge-bot: bridge created -> conference 10.0.0.45:8030. Paging on-call escalation to infra-sre.

ajay (oncall): handoff to infra-sre @maria. I'm going to run a rolling restart of the pool after draining and then re-enable limited capacity with lower concurrency. Leaving oncall but switching to watches.

maria (infra): kernel logs snapshot:
```
[ 3456.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:4b:00): 31, PID=2234, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 3456.123457] <kernel>: BUG: scheduling while atomic: attempt to free pinned pages during DPDK-like path?
[ 3456.123500] device driver oom: illegal read at 0x7ffe...
```
Looks like a driver/kernel-level fault triggered by an out-of-bounds DMA into host pinned memory — suspect race in runtime's pin/unpin lifecycle.

kelsey (runtime): confirmed repro locally with a stress harness: repeated hot swap of tensor buffers + eviction leads to use-after-free in our pinned slab allocator. Repro steps and stack attached to the bug tracker. We'll roll a 2-line revert to stop pooling; then schedule a fix that adds refcounts and a small epoch-based grace window.

liz_sre: Customer comms: CS drafted message noting degraded performance and retries for a small subset of customers, ETA for full mitigation is 45m. No SLA breach expected if we maintain fallback to cpu variant.

ajay (oncall): ops tasks completed: cordoned node, drained, forced restart of driver. scaled down pool to 50% capacity. Flag change applied to configmap; rolling restart of runtime pods started.

deploy-bot: configmap updated at 2026-03-10T14:34:10Z by kelsey. RollingRestart job created for serving-runtime (batch=10).

maria (infra): node reboot completed, driver reloaded. Observed one more driver-reset but no kernel panic. Starting to bring back small batches of pods to the pool with `max_concurrency=2`.

kelsey (runtime): hotfix deployed (disable pooling). Logs show illegal address errors stop for newly-started pods. Older in-memory processes still show crashes; those were replaced during drain. Confirming via metrics: error-rate dropped from 12% -> 0.6% over 12 minutes.

liz_sre: CS sent initial status update to impacted customers at 14:38Z. Preparing a post-incident note with technical summary and next steps.

ajay (oncall): handing off to maria for follow-ups and deep-dive. I'll remain available. Next oncall @liz_sre will watch customer comms.

maria (infra): Next steps: 1) run full replay workload on staging with new hotfix to ensure no regression; 2) create kernel/driver reproducer for vendor; 3) schedule a proper fix in runtime repo to add refcount/epoch; 4) plan canary rollout for the fix with perf guardrails.

kelsey (runtime): created CH-1482 with repro, PR with revert hotfix merged to canary branch. We'll run perf tests to quantify throughput loss; early numbers show ~8-12% throughput drop under heavy load.

ops-bridge-bot: incident tagged as "mitigated" at 2026-03-10T15:06:40Z. Keeping thread open for RCA items and vendor engagement.

liz_sre: scheduling RCA meeting for 2026-03-11 09:00Z PST. Responsibilities assigned: maria (kernel/drivers), kelsey (runtime fix & perf), ajay (mitigations & runbook updates), liz_sre (customer postmortem).

ajay (oncall): quick note: add runbook step to prefer model fallback route when node-level driver resets exceed 3 within 10m. That prevented a wider outage today.

kelsey (runtime): adding test harness for pinned allocator races; will include in CI gating.

maria (infra): filing vendor bug to GPU vendor with kernel logs and reproducer. Attaching `dmesg`, `journalctl`, and the stress harness.

liz_sre: closing customer incident loop once postmortem is published. Thanks everyone for fast coordination :heartpulse:

ajay (oncall): note timestamping: root alert generated at 1769129999. closing active oncall actions at 1769133600.

(threads/attachments: kernel logs, stack traces, PR links, and customer comms drafts attached in thread replies)
